headline: Requests for two Moody Street businesses to appear over police-reported incidents were dismissed.
summary: The Deep Elm request, at 484 Moody Street, concerned a fight outside the business on October 25, 2026, under report number 260-35846. The Shaqui Shalom request, at 342 Moody Street, concerned a customer found unresponsive, reported on October 31, 2026, under report number 260 36595. Also approved were a change of manager at 123 Moody Street, ownership changes at Moody Spa, and an extra hour on New Year's Eve for various licenses.
decisions: Approved a one-day beer and wine permit for Megan McKenna's family Christmas party on December 13.
Approved ownership, officer, and manager changes for UMA Convenience, doing business as Moody Spa, at 811 Moody Street.
Approved a change of manager, to Richard Brackett, for the business at 123 Moody Street.
Approved the license meeting dates for 2027.
Approved the 2027 renewals of common victualler and liquor licenses.
Approved an extra hour on New Year's Eve, until 2 a.m., for the various licenses read aloud.
Dismissed the request for Deep Elm, 484 Moody Street, to appear over an October 25, 2026 police report.
Dismissed the request for Shaqui Shalom, 342 Moody Street, to appear over an October 31, 2026 police report.
discussion: Deep Elm incident: The police report described a dispute over a plate and drinks, a shove, and a slap outside. The video showed a heated argument, but sun glare blocked the view of the doorway. Commissioners advised calling police instead of confronting customers.

Shaqui Shalom incident: The police report said a customer passed out after a shot of vodka and was taken to the hospital. The business was advised to stop serving anyone who seems intoxicated and to call police if a customer refuses to leave.

Guadalotania Inc. license hearing: A public hearing covered a new common victualler and liquor license at 581 Moody Street. The applicant described a small menu of Central American dishes, such as pupusas and tortillas.
